Hi everyone, we’ve got some new information for Matt’s upcoming and latest release in the DCC series.   
Check out the ACE cover art for the hardcover edition of A Parade of Horribles!
This highly anticipated continuation of the explosive and emotionally charged cliffhangers godslapping us in book 7 has us hostage. We’re holding our breath and on the edge of our seat. Bask in the glory!   
We’re incredibly excited to share this new cover and the release schedule with the community.  
Additionally, for fans of the classic cover art styles, the limited edition Luciano Fleitas trade paperback version is coming soon.   
For those who love the old school style cover art, we got you, ah, well, covered.   
Stay tuned for more info on that edition, which should be revealed sometime in the coming weeks.
We’re incredibly excited to see what Luciano has created for the paperback edition.   
Finally, for those who want the format release schedule at a glance – please refer to the numbered list below. We’ve set this list of quick links to what we have thus far.   
We’ll keep you updated as we get more info!
Release Dates, formats, and Pre-order options
Update: All versions will release on May 12, 2026.
1. The ebook is available for pre-order here.
2. Audible has the audiobook available for pre-order now!.
3. The hardcover edition is available for pre-order via Ace Publishing.
4. Additionally, there is a limited print run of trade paperback copies slated with the Luciano Fleitas cover. These are only available directly from Grim Oak Press.   
You can pre-order the Luciano version here!  
If you ever bought anything from the Signed Page, they’re the same, amazing people.  
They’re a joy to work with. Show them love!
5. Invitation bookshop is also offered limited run signed copies – you can find more about their signed copies via the Parade of Horribles pre-order page for the shop!
Make sure to keep an eye on Matt’s dedicated APOH book page and the bookstore pages for the updated options when they become available!
As we have more info, we’ll pass it along.
The Gargler
New Achievement
Sit down, crawler, and let me tell you a story.
It was a cold Thursday evening in December. The heat clicked on in a cozy recording studio in Kansas City, Missouri. The computer on the desk hummed happily away, the fluorescent lights buzzed, and the microphone hung patiently waiting for its master to return.
This innocent little studio was unprepared for the carnage that was about to occur within its walls.
Floors splattered in goop.
Rugs permanently stained.
Walls covered in spittle and the last vestiges of a narrator’s pride.
Thick white loads flying through the air.
Not even the poor monitors were spared.
This, my friends, was the Day of the Yogurt.
“But how?” I hear you ask, “How did this recording studio come to be covered in so much dairy product?”
To answer that we must turn to the unholy scripture itself. Do you ever read a line in one of those books about my dungeon and think to yourself, “wow, this author has some sort of freaky sadomasochistic relationship with his narrator.” You know the ones I’m talking about. That gremlin on the fourth floor whose inflection is like a Creole guy poorly attempting a cockney accent. That weird fucking thing with the nipples. Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang somehow sounding like that Oshira guy and Texan Jesus at the same time.
And, of course, a giant talking penis with a voice like that of a big, beefy wrestler trying to shout while gargling messily on something thick.
The lucky few who were watching the livestream that day will never forget the sight of highly respected narrator Jeff Hays making a mess of himself worthy of a PornHub star.
Let it never be said that Jeff isn’t dedicated to his craft. Nor that my creator isn’t just as much of a sadistic bastard as I am.
You’ve received a 5.3oz container of Thick & Creamy Low Fat Skyr Yogurt (Strawberry & Lingonberry Flavor). Don’t choke on it!
Close
I Found it Hard, it’s Hard to Find
New Achievement!
You’ve accidentally clicked on exactly the right set of pixels on this page to trigger a secret achievement! That, or you’re one of those holier-than-thou assholes who only uses the keyboard and has the Vimium extension installed on your browser. We get it, you’re soooooo much more efficient than all these other plebians still piddling around with mice. Or maybe you just used the Inspector like a cheating little bitch.
Either way, you found an Easter egg! Specifically, you’ve found the egg that contains my personal (and correct) opinions on vinyl players and IPAs. Spoiler alert: they both suck.
You’ve received the audio of a skit staring yours truly! This skit was previously only found on the NYCC-exclusive First Edition Vinyl of the Dungeon Crawler Carl Audio Immersion Tunnel OST. Only a hundred of these exist in this world, so unless you’ve got a time machine you’re shit out of luck on acquiring one. Consider this your consolation prize.
Audio Transcript
Carl: Hey Donut, check it out. Soundbooth Theater finally got off their asses and made an original soundtrack.  
Donut: Oh my gosh! Really?  
Carl: And, you’re going to love this, it’s an exclusive New York Comic Con-only edition. That’s the only place people can get this. It’s the amazing original music from the Immersion Tunnel version of SoundBooth Theater’s production of Dungeon Crawler Carl Season 1. Season 2 is coming soon.  
Donut: This is great! The Princess Posse is going to be so excited. They love exclusive items. Let me see it! Let me see it! Mongo, come here, mommy has exclusive merch! She has an album.  
Mongo: \screech\  
Donut: Look, Mongo, it’s it great? Wait. Carl, what is that thing?  
Carl: It’s a vinyl. A record. For record players?  
Donut: I know what vinyl is, Carl. Just because I wasn’t born in the eighteen hundreds doesn’t mean I don’t know what a vinyl is. I’ve watched the History Channel. No wait, is it a record that’s really hiding a USB thingy? Or is it a link to Spotify?  
Carl: No, it’s an actual record.  
Donut: What? Why? Is there a CD version?  
Carl: No, Donut, this is it. This is the album. Did you know last year more people bought vinyls than-  
The AI: New Achievement! Shag Carpet.  
The AI (sexy 70s voice): Okay, picture this: it’s 1978. You’re in your fly bachelor pad with a hot little somethin-somethin. You’ve just cracked open an ice-cold Michelob and you are about to get. It. On. “Sorry babe, it’s been 25 minutes, I gotta turn the record over, ya dig? Maybe quit bouncin’ around so much, you’re making my hi-fi skip.”  
The AI: You have collected the single least convenient, most cock-blocking method of music storage in history and convinced yourself it’s somehow superior to literally everything else that has come since! “ThE qUaLiTy Is BeTtEr.” Shut the fuck up hipster, we’ve all moved on. You know what? IPAs suck too. Why don’t you go gentrify a poor neighborhood with an over-priced farmer’s market and hot yoga studio. Reward: you’ve received a bucket of ethically sourced vegan beard oil.  
Carl: Jeez. That was a little harsh. I like IPAs.  
Donut: See? See?! Mongo, mommy apologizes for getting your hopes up.  
Mongo: \screech\  
Carl: Hm. Well, I think it’s cool. I heard they’re going to be doing more of these soon. And I’m sure if I actually had a record player to listen to this thing with, the music would be great.
Close

Matt Dinniman

Dungeon Crawler Carl #8
A Parade of Horribles
It’s off to the races in the explosive 8th book in the Dungeon Crawler Carl series!
As chaos and mass panic spread outside the dungeon in the wake of Faction Wars, Carl and Donut find themselves on the tenth floor, where they’re forced to compete in a surprisingly normal set of tasks. Well, normal for the dungeon.
Races. Get from point A to point B, and don’t come in last. After each race, they pick an upgrade for their vehicle and the track gets more challenging. It all seems a little too normal, a little too simple.
READ MORE
Ignore those strange glitches that are occurring with increasing frequency. Don’t listen to those whispers about what’s happening on the mysterious eleventh floor, something the system AI calls A Parade of Horribles. Nobody, not even the showrunners, knows what that means. Just that the AI has ominously dubbed it “a coming-out party for the ages.”
Everything is fine, Crawler. I repeat, everything is fine.
Carl hates that it’s business as usual. The rules of this floor have taken away his agency. That just will not do.
So Carl is planning a party of his own. It’s a plan so dangerous, so insane, he can’t even consult his friends lest the AI put a stop to it. Because if it goes wrong, it’s not just the end of Carl and Donut. No. The stakes are higher than they’ve ever been.
Published May 12, 2026
EDITIONS:
The Dungeon Crawler Carl Series
Join Coast Guard vet Carl and his ex-girlfriend’s cat, Princess Donut, as they try to survive the end of the world—or just get to the next level—in a video game–like, trap-filled fantasy dungeon.

The New Dungeon Crawler Carl Book Is Out Today on All Formats
It's off to the races.
Jacob Kienlen Avatar

The Dungeon Crawler Carl series has been experiencing a whirlwind of a year so far in 2026. The live-action TV series was officially confirmed for Peacock, a massive tabletop RPG was announced, and Playmates even revealed a new toy line. If you weren't already a fan of Matt Dinniman's LitRPG phenomenon, there's never been a better time to jump on the bandwagon.
For those who are already fully caught up on the series, however, there's a new book out today! A Parade of Horribles is the eighth Dungeon Crawler Carl book so far, it's been released as an eBook, audiobook, and a hardcover edition all at once. Here's everything you need to know before you buy.
Where to Buy A Parade of Horribles
A Parade of Horribles
A Parade of Horribles
Dungeon Crawler Carl is one of my favorite LitRPG books, and since A Parade of Horribles is available with my Kindle Unlimited subscription, it's going to be a day one read for me. The Kindle version is the best deal overall if you don't have a subscription, but for the first time ever you can also purchase the hardcover edition on release day.
I checked various retailers and Amazon has the best discount overall on physical copies compared to other major online bookstores. Amazon won't be able to deliver your copy immediately, however, so Barnes & Noble is your best bet if you want to be able to pick it up first thing today at your local store.
Note: Kindle books usually release at midnight ET in the U.S.
The audiobook version is available too
A Parade of Horribles (Audiobook)
A Parade of Horribles (Audiobook)
For fans of the audiobook versions of Dungeon Crawler Carl, you can also start listening to the Audible edition today. You don't have to have an Audible subscription to purchase the audiobook, which is discounted to $18.86 on Amazon right now. There are free trials available for Audible that grant you a first credit alongside 30-days of access to other benefits of the service.
If you haven't listened to the audiobook versions of Dungeon Crawler Carl yet, I'd highly recommend checking them out. There's a reason it's one of the most popular audiobooks currently running.
What's A Parade of Horribles About?
Carl and Donut are deep in the dungeon now, and things are going to continue to get weird. If you're wondering what to expect, here's a quick synopsis directly from Matt Dinniman's website:
"As chaos and mass panic spread outside the dungeon in the wake of Faction Wars, Carl and Donut find themselves on the tenth floor, where they’re forced to compete in a surprisingly normal set of tasks. Well, normal for the dungeon.
Races. Get from point A to point B, and don’t come in last. After each race, they pick an upgrade for their vehicle and the track gets more challenging. It all seems a little too normal, a little too simple."
If you want a more detailed sample of the story, you can check out an excerpt from the book from IGN's interview with the author.

It’s off to the races in the explosive eighth book in the Dungeon Crawler Carl series.
As chaos and mass panic spread outside the dungeon in the wake of Faction Wars, Carl and Donut find themselves on the tenth floor, where they’re forced to compete in a surprisingly normal set of tasks. Well, normal for the dungeon.
Races. Get from point A to point B, and don’t come in last. After each race, they pick an upgrade for their vehicle and the track gets more challenging. It all seems a little too normal, a little too simple.
Ignore those strange glitches that are occurring with increasing frequency. Don’t listen to those whispers about what’s happening on the mysterious eleventh floor, something the system AI calls A Parade of Horribles. Nobody, not even the showrunners, knows what that means. Just that the AI has ominously dubbed it “a coming-out party for the ages.”
Everything is fine, Crawler. I repeat, everything is fine.
Carl hates that it’s business as usual. The rules of this floor have taken away his agency. That just will not do.
So Carl is planning a party of his own. It’s a plan so dangerous, so insane, he can’t even consult his friends lest the AI put a stop to it. Because if it goes wrong, it’s not just the end of Carl and Donut. No. The stakes are higher than they’ve ever been.
